title: Hail! Father, Son, and Holy Ghost
description: Hail! Father, Son, and Holy Ghost in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 239.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hail! Fa-ther, Son, and Ho-ly Ghost, One God, in Per-sons Three! Of Thee we make our joy-ful boast, Our songs we make of Thee.

lines: Hail! Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Of Thee we make our joyful boast,
Our songs we make of Thee.
Thou neither canst be felt nor seen;
Beyond the bounds of time and space,
Thine eye doth all things see;
And every thought of every heart
Whate'er thou wilt, in earth below
But chiefly we rejoice to know
Thou lov'st whate'er thy hands have made,
Mercy, with love and endless grace,
O'er all thy works doth reign;
But mostly thou delight'st to bless
But, chiefly, Lord, the thanks receive,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
